title: NCHR Statement on IHC Ruling on Enforced Disappearances
publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
claim: NCHR said the IHC treated enforced disappearances as a 'seemingly undeclared tacit policy of the state' and welcomed the court's order holding chief executives and interior ministers, past and present, accountable, while also welcoming the government's committee on the issue.
source_confidence_reason: Official statutory human-rights body summarizing the court ruling and government response.
ruler_attribution: Strong for attribution of Sharif's government as the addressed authority; weak for proving personal operational direction.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not identify which security actors carried out individual disappearances.

title: Pakistan: Braving the Storm: Enforced disappearances and the right to protest in Pakistan
claim: Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.
source_confidence_reason: Independent rights report with a clear 2022 scope and specific abuse pattern.
ruler_attribution: Supports a state-abuse pattern under Sharif's term, but it does not by itself prove his personal ordering of each incident.
contrary_evidence: The report attributes the abuses to state forces generally, not to Sharif personally.

title: IHC orders inquiry into claims of torture on Gill
claim: The Islamabad High Court ordered the federal government and interior secretary to appoint an inquiry officer into allegations that PTI leader Shahbaz Gill was tortured in police custody, and ordered SSP-level supervision to ensure no further torture.
locator: report of the IHC order and the court's directions
source_confidence_reason: Court order summarized by a mainstream local outlet; the underlying court record is the stronger source but was not directly accessible here.
ruler_attribution: Directly implicates the police custody chain during Sharif's government, but not a proven personal order by Sharif.
contrary_evidence: Police and government officials denied torture; the dispute remained under inquiry.

title: Press Release: NCHR Inquiry Report on Custodial Torture at Central Jail (Adiala), Rawalpindi
publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
claim: NCHR said its Adiala Jail inquiry found 74% of interviewed inmates alleging torture and 100% reporting financial extortion for access to basic facilities, and the court ordered the report shared with the PM and cabinet for immediate action against responsible public servants.
locator: paragraphs describing the inquiry findings and court directions
source_confidence_reason: Official inquiry report announcement with concrete findings and a court-ordered response chain.
ruler_attribution: Strong for prison administration under the federal government; still indirect for naming Sharif as the actor behind abuse.
contrary_evidence: The report describes jail conditions and responsible public servants, not a personal PM order.

title: Alvi concerned over treatment of journalists
claim: President Arif Alvi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing deep concern over harassment of journalists, citing arrests, beatings, harassment, and sedition cases meant to create fear and terror, and urging immediate remedial action and protection from security agencies.
locator: Dawn summary of the president's letter
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct written notice to Sharif from the head of state.
ruler_attribution: This is direct notice to Sharif and his government; it still does not prove he personally directed the harassment.
contrary_evidence: The letter is a warning and request, not proof of authorial control over every abuse.

title: NCHR launches complaint cell for women journalists
claim: NCHR launched a complaint cell for women journalists after a consultative meeting with women journalists from across Pakistan, citing online violence, harassment, attack risks, and censorship against women reporters.
locator: article body describing the launch and the consultative meeting
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of an official human-rights initiative with specific abuse descriptions.
ruler_attribution: Useful as evidence of a documented abuse environment and institutional response; the PM link remains indirect unless paired with the president's letter.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish direct PM-level authorship of the abuse campaigns.

title: NCHR launches fact finding report on minority rights
claim: NCHR's minority report said nearly half of reserved minority posts were vacant, 80% of non-Muslims in filled posts were in BPS 01-04, and the Ministry of Human Rights sent letters to provincial chief secretaries directing them to protect minority rights.
source_confidence_reason: Official news service reporting a government-linked rights report and subsequent ministry action to provinces.
ruler_attribution: Strong for provincial policy action under Sharif's federal government; weak for proving personal day-to-day management.
contrary_evidence: The report reflects longstanding structural discrimination and does not isolate Sharif as the sole cause.
